ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, officers, and commercial counterparties against the Consolidated United Nations Security Council Sanctions List, Canadian sanctions imposed under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act, the OSFI/Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and Canada's Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) definitions under FINTRAC rules. Ongoing enhanced due diligence is required for high-risk jurisdictions and for any person with ownership or control over the limited partnership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises (REQ) online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the legal name of a Quebec enterprise must be French or contain French phrasing. Chinese brand transliteration into Latin characters is permitted provided the name is drafted to be legally and linguistically acceptable in French; where the desired brand is a registered foreign trademark, the trademark may form part of the name, but the corporate name must include a French descriptive element. Any Chinese characters must be transliterated, and French must be the prevailing language of the registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, the applicant shall receive a written refusal specifying the legal grounds, typically similarity with an existing distinctive name or non-compliance with the Charter of the French Language. The applicant may either file a revised name and new clearance request, or submit a formal written reconsideration to the REQ within 30 days with supplemental arguments and factual explanations. If the reconsideration is denied, judicial/administrative appeal may be brought before the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) or the Superior Court of Quebec on arguable legal grounds, subject to a strict 30-day appellate window. Practical recommendation: secure preliminary confidential name search before formal submission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual-only mailing address will not be accepted as the registered establishment in Quebec; the limited partnership must maintain a real physical place of business or a registered office provided by a licensed resident service provider. A professional registered agent's physical office is acceptable for compliance purposes, but the alcohol export operation should maintain genuine commercial substance at a Quebec physical location to support the related import/export liquor licence and goods and services tax (GST) registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236 et seq. (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. C-4.1, ss. 1 to 19; Business Corporations Act (Québec) if the general partner is a legal person
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises — Registrar of Enterprises, Gouvernement du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation — Initial Declaration of Registration for a société en commandite / limited partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital under Quebec law; capital contributions are fixed contractually in the limited partnership agreement with no statutory escrow account requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of [Corporate General Partner], acting for and on behalf of the [LP Name], s.e.c., hereby subscribes to the partnership interests and capital commitments set out in the Initial Declaration and Limited Partnership Agreement; RESOLVED, that the registered and head office of the Partnership be established and maintained at [full address], Quebec, with all books and records located there; RESOLVED, that [name] be and is hereby appointed Manager and Attorney-in-fact, authorized to file the Declaration of Registration, open segregated bank accounts, engage counsel, and obtain alcohol export permits; and RESOLVED, that all capital contributions be held segregated until legal publicity is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Clearance and Pre-registration Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises — Online Services Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search of the enterprise name in the Québec enterprise register using the proposed limited partnership name; check that the name includes the required legal designation 's.e.c.' or 'SEC' for société en commandite, does not create confusion with a prior registered name or trademark, and does not falsely imply corporate status; obtain written consent if the name includes a third person's name; document the name choice in the partnership agreement.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name and legal designation
Copy of the corporate general partner's constitution/act if applicable
Consent letters from persons whose names appear in the partnership name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, file a revised name containing a distinctive element or a registration number component and resubmit; attach a consent letter or explanatory affidavit to cure any anonymity or conflict issue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des notaires du Québec / Legal Counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement in English or French, specifying the general partner (gérant), limited partners, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratio, management authority, Quebec head office, and dissolution rules; ensure the agreement is signed by all general and limited partners; attend before a notary if real property rights, inheritance planning, or enhanced evidentiary certainty is required; keep an original executed copy as a governing record.
required_dossiers: Resolution of the corporate general partner approving the partnership formation
Proof of authority and signature specimens of each partner
Power of attorney for any partner signing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect in partner consent or contribution is later alleged, execute a unanimous retroactive corrective agreement; if notarization is required for registration of a related immovable, coordinate re-execution before a notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Limited Partnership with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises — Québec Central Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Initial Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) online or by mail with the Registraire des entreprises; include the partnership name, Quebec head-office address, date of establishment, precise business activity code (ISIC 4632 / NAICS 424820), identification of the general partner, and the amount and nature of partner contributions; pay the filing fee and obtain the Québec enterprise number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Consent letter of the registered office/head-office premises
Identification record of the general partner and each limited partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a notice of incompleteness or refusal, amend the declaration and return the missing attachments within 15 days; where the general partner is domiciled outside Quebec, provide a valid agent for service of process declaration and a certificate of registration from its home province.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Tax Registration and Business Number Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued NEQ, register the limited partnership for Québec Sales Tax (QST) and Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) with Revenu Québec; confirm the partnership's wholesale distribution activity is listed under NAICS 424820 / ISIC 4632; provide banking information for Canadian-dollar accounts; obtain a CRA business number if the partnership also engages in excise-related transactions as a bonded warehouse operator.
required_dossiers: NEQ assignment notice from the Registraire des entreprises
General partner's identification and Quebec tax accounts
Completed Revenu Québec registration form or online attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec queries the registration because no immediate taxable supply exists, submit a statement of anticipated wholesale operations and liquor export contracts; if GST/HST export exemptions are claimed, maintain evidence of shipment out of Canada.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Premises Lease, Municipal Business Permit and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipality / Service de sécurité incendie / CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a warehouse or office space zoned for wholesale alcoholic beverage storage and distribution; obtain the municipal business authorization (certificat d'autorisation) for warehousing; schedule a fire-safety and occupational-health inspection with the local fire service and CNESST; implement a floor-load compliance certification for palletized crates and storage racks; ensure approved fire-suppression and spill-containment systems are installed before physical operations commence.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or certificate of title for the Quebec premises
Municipal zoning and building occupancy certificate
CNESST self-inspection questionnaire and fire-safety certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal zoning prohibits the intended alcohol warehouse use, apply for a minor variance (dérogation mineure) or identify a compliant alternative location; if the fire inspection identifies deficiencies, remedy the protected flooring, exhaust, sprinkler or egress issues and request reinspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux (RACJ) in coordination with the Société des alcools du Québec (SAQ) and the Canada Revenue Agency, Excise Act, 2001 licensing regime
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Québec alcoholic beverage supplier/exporter authorization and federal excise bonded warehouse registration for duty-deferred storage and export

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — non-listed warehousing and wholesale distribution activity under Section 31 of the Environment Quality Act (EQA); no mandatory full EIA or environmental authorization is required absent a discharge to water, uncontained emissions, or a quantified threshold exceeding applicable regulation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero-discharge stormwater and housekeeping plan; volatile organic compound emissions maintained below the Clean Air Act permitting threshold; ethanol spills and container rinsings captured and disposed of as hazardous waste; aboveground alcohol storage provided with secondary containment; compliance with municipal sewer discharge limits if any wastewater is generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire-safety certificate issued by the local fire prevention service under the Quebec Building Code; CNESST workplace-safety clearance; structural-load inspection for pallet racking and storage shelves; emergency exits and sprinkler compliance; spill-containment training and SDS sheets available in French; electrical and ventilation certificates for the storage area.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal income, GST/HST and excise duty administration: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) with the Business Registration Online portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Quebec sales tax (QST) administration: Revenu Québec (https://www.revenuquebec.ca) in coordination with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec for the enterprise number (NEQ); customs and export reporting: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CES); provincial liquor control for exporting spirits from Quebec: Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux (RACJ) and, where relevant, Société des alcools du Québec (SAQ) permit controls.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Quebec limited partnership: (1) register the LP with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (declaration of immatriculation) to obtain the NEQ; (2) register the federal Business Number (BN) with CRA Business Registration Online, selecting RP (GST/HST), RC (payroll if employees exist) and RD (Excise Duty framework under the Excise Act, 2001); (3) register for QST at Revenu Québec through the enterprise registration module; GST/QST registration is mandatory once the LP's taxable supplies exceed C$30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the four trailing consecutive calendar quarters, or earlier when the LP imports commercial goods into Quebec or otherwise carries on a Quebec enterprise; (4) obtain the RACJ exporter's liquor permit and, when duty deferral is desired, an excise warehouse licence or an excise-drawback exporter designation from CRA Excise Duty; (5) complete CBSA exporter registration linked to the BN for electronic export declarations. The non-resident Chinese partners need not be listed in the BN file, but the general partner acts as the LP's administrative representative and must identify itself and the LP to CRA and Revenu Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; Territorial_Scope: under Income Tax Act (Canada) s. 96 and Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 599, the limited partnership is fiscally transparent and is not an income taxpayer; each partner pays tax on its distributive share of the LP's Quebec business income. Canadian-resident partners pay tax on worldwide income; non-resident (Chinese) partners are liable for Canadian Part I tax only on Canadian-source partnership income (Income Tax Act s. 2(3), s. 115 and s. 212(13.1) for amounts flowing out of the partnership), with parallel Quebec rules. For GST/QST the LP itself is a separate 'person' and the registrant, entitled to claim input tax credits on purchases of Baijiu inventory, warehousing, freight and marketing services. Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable in Quebec for export distribution; export relief is achieved through statutory zero-rating and excise drawback rather than through any geographic zone exemption. Entity_Level_Taxation: not applicable at the LP level for income tax purposes, but the LP is the entity-level registrant for GST, QST and excise purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada and Quebec do not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' entity classification election; partnership transparency is mandatory. Available elections and designations relevant to this LP include: (i) voluntary GST/QST registration election for a small supplier under Excise Tax Act s. 240(3) and QSTA art. 259, permitting early input tax credit recovery before crossing the C$30,000 threshold; (ii) rollover election under Income Tax Act s. 97(2) and Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 729 on the transfer of Baijiu inventory, warehouse leases and distribution contracts into the LP at tax cost; (iii) designation of the general partner as the tax-matters partner so that the federal BN and QST number are consolidated in a single filing profile; (iv) for excise duty purposes, election to operate as a licensed excise warehouse user or to claim monthly duty drawback on exported spirits instead of paying duty upon import; (v) with Chinese partners present, the LP must maintain contemporaneous documentation that no hybrid-mismatch double deduction arises (Income Tax Act ss. 18.4 and 94.2, and the excessive interest and financing expenses limitation rules) and may elect to compute Part XIII non-resident withholding on the LP's net allocable amounts payable to non-resident partners.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT-type regime: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% under the Excise Tax Act, Parts V-IX, plus the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.975% under the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax (CQLR c. T-0.1), producing a combined headline rate of 14.975%; in addition, the federal Excise Act, 2001 imposes an annually indexed spirits duty per litre of absolute ethyl alcohol, and Quebec applies a domestic beverage alcohol contribution and SAQ markup on liquor delivered for consumption in Quebec; both are relieved on compliant export through duty-free excise warehouse movement or drawback.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or across the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters (GST: Excise Tax Act s. 148; QST: QSTA art. 259). Mandatory earlier registration applies to any non-resident importing commercial goods (including Baijiu) into Quebec or carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment, warehouse, or agent. The voluntary small-supplier registration threshold is likewise C$30,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time tax-authority clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) e-invoicing. Obligations are record-based: every registrant must issue a compliant invoice stating the supplier's BN, the LP's legal name, date, description and quantity of Baijiu, unit price, GST and QST indicated separately or an explicit zero-rated/export notation, and must retain all electronic records for six years (Excise Tax Act s. 286(2)). Revenu Québec requires electronic filing and payment for most QST registrants and accepts PEPPOL UBL 2.1 e-invoices. Mandatory digital transmission applies to customs and trade data: CBSA eManifest/PARS for imports and the Canadian Export Reporting System (CES) for the LP's export declarations, which constitute the legally authoritative outward clearance records. No tax-authority pre-approval of invoices is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registrant's supply of Baijiu made in Quebec to a non-resident buyer is zero-rated for GST and QST under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI, Part V (supply of goods that are exported) and the parallel QST zero-rating, provided that: (i) physical export occurs as soon as possible after the supply and, in administrative practice, within 60 days of transfer of possession; (ii) the LP retains shipping, customs, and payment evidence establishing that the goods left Canada and entered the named foreign market; (iii) title and risk of loss pass to the foreign buyer at or before export; (iv) for Baijiu previously imported from China, the import entry is matched to the export entry and the goods are not diverted to Quebec consumption; (v) federal spirits excise duty is relieved by exporting from a licensed excise warehouse (duty-unpaid movement) or by a drawback claim under the Excise Act, 2001, and the RACJ export permit declares the withdrawal so that no Quebec beverage markup applies; (vi) incidental logistics and freight services supplied to the non-resident buyer in respect of the exported goods are separately zero-rated only if supplied directly to the non-resident and performed in respect of the exported Baijiu.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13 Export Declaration filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CES), reflecting the LP's Business Number, destination port, HS code 2208.90 (Chinese Baijiu), quantity, alcoholic strength, and invoice value

Original or certified electronic Bill of Lading (ocean/air/rail or combined transport bill) proving physical movement of the container from Canada to the named foreign destination with the Baijiu consignee identified in the destination country

Inward Remittance Certificate or bank confirmation of settlement (SWIFT MT103 trace or letter-of-credit negotiation record) evidencing receipt of export proceeds by the LP within 180 days of the export date
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec jointly audit export zero-rating and excise drawback files; the burden of proof is on the LP to produce the complete documentation bundle with matching inventory movement within the six-year record-retention window. A confirmed export substantiation failure triggers reversal of the zero-rating, immediate reassessment of 5% GST plus 9.975% QST on the export invoice value, reassessment of federal spirits excise duty with interest, and denial or recapture of related input tax credits and duty drawback. Civil penalties include a 25% gross-negligence penalty on federal tax (Excise Tax Act s. 285(1)), a 50% penalty for false statements or omissions made with intent (s. 280), QST penalties under QSTA arts. 1012, 1015 and 1016 (25%-50% tiers), and a 50% anti-avoidance penalty under the Excise Act, 2001 for fabricated export documentation. Criminal exposure includes fines up to C$50,000 and imprisonment for excise offences (Excise Act, 2001 s. 218), and liability under Criminal Code s. 380(1) fraud where export claims are materially false. The general partner of the Quebec LP bears unlimited joint and several liability for all such clawbacks; normal four-year reassessment limits do not apply where misrepresentation or fraud is established; SAQ/RACJ export permits are suspended immediately upon diversion of goods to the domestic Quebec market, and diverted goods are forfeited with duty and taxes payable as if domestically released.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada has no centralized exchange-control ministry; cross-border payment review is distributed among these federal authorities, with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administering physical cross-border currency reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully convertible on both current and capital account under IMF Article VIII. There is no Canadian foreign-exchange control regime, no prior exchange-control approval for capital injection, and no administrative limit on profit remittance or capital repatriation. Remittance of distributable profits from a Quebec Limited Partnership to non-resident partners is governed by the limited partnership agreement, solvency requirements, Part XIII non-resident withholding tax rules, and FATCA/CRS documentation obligations. Banks will impose independent AML/EDD review on all high-value wires but no exchange-control permit is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement exists in Canada. Exporters may retain baijiu export receipts in foreign currency, hold them in foreign-currency bank accounts, or convert them to Canadian dollars at commercial rates without a mandatory timeline or conversion ratio. All cross-border currency or monetary instruments of C$10,000 or more must be reported to CBSA/FINTRAC, and international wire instructions are subject to FINTRAC transaction-reporting obligations when filing thresholds are met; exporters must also retain trade documentation under customs and income-tax record-keeping rules.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-medium. Foreign digital EMIs may function as supplementary payment collection and low-value disbursement rails in Canada only if they are registered with FINTRAC as money service businesses under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and comply with applicable Quebec money-services business requirements. They cannot lawfully take Canadian deposits, issue commercial letters of credit, or act as the primary treasury counterparty for a capital-escrow structure. EMIs may be acceptable for sub-C$100,000 open-account trade disbursements where full transaction transparency exists, but the Quebec LP must maintain a Schedule I bank account as the principal liquidity concentration point.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is not a universal statutory requirement, but in practice Quebec Schedule I banks require at least one signing general partner or authorized agent to complete an in-person or video-verified KYC interview. Remote account opening is possible where the LP is registered in Quebec, a Canadian registered office exists, certified identity documents are provided, and the bank's enhanced due diligence process applies. For a non-resident-controlled LP, especially one with PRC partners and a spirits-export mandate, a physical meeting at a Quebec branch materially reduces onboarding delay and is strongly recommended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a non-resident PRC individual or related-party exporter routed through a third-party intermediary or family member account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Quebec limited partnership agreement; capital call notices and LP subscription ledger; source-of-funds affidavit for each limited partner; bank reference letters; six-month personal or corporate bank statements for the remitting entity; registry extracts showing ultimate beneficial ownership; commercial master supply agreement demonstrating the upstream baijiu procurement relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Repeated round-number USD or RMB trade invoices for baijiu at valuations markedly above or below market benchmarks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Manufacturer's official price list; ISO 22000 and food-safety certifications; Chinese customs export declarations; CBSA import entry filings; bills of lading or airway bills; warehouse receipts; insurance certificates; independent third-party inspection reports; and a written internal transfer-pricing memo explaining the commercial mark-up.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of regulated fintech wallets or payment cards for trade settlement, especially splitting payments to stay below reporting thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete invoice-by-invoice reconciliation; counterparty KYC summaries; sanctions and PEP screening logs from the LP's compliance system; evidence that each payment corresponds to a discrete commercial contract; signed payment-processing agreement with the fintech provider; and board-approved treasury policy prohibiting structuring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid in-and-out flow in the capital escrow account that does not match the subscribed capital schedule or appears to be a pass-through payments hub.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow undertaking signed by the partnership and depositing bank; subscriber ledger and committed-capital schedule; board or GP resolutions authorizing disbursements; fully traced funds-flow statement matching each disbursement to an invoice or closing item; updated CRS/FATCA self-certifications; and legal opinion confirming that LP interests are not marketed to retail investors in a manner requiring securities registration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions to the Quebec LP must be settled through the international banking system using SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the LP's Canadian capital escrow account at a Schedule I bank. Remittance instructions must identify the remitter, the LP entity name, and the purpose as 'Capital contribution to CA_LP under LP Agreement dated [date]'. Bank verification will include a copy of the LP agreement, beneficial-ownership certification, CRS self-certification, and source-of-funds evidence. Canada imposes no exchange-control permit requirement, but the wire must not be artificially split below C$10,000 to avoid FINTRAC/CBSA cross-border reporting; transactions must be routed through the originating bank's direct correspondent relationship into the Canadian bank's SWIFT BIC and domestic clearing via Payments Canada.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for baijiu procurement and logistics should be cleared through a tiered rail structure. For documentary trade, the Canadian bank issues or advises a commercial letter of credit via SWIFT MT700 under UCP600; settlement occurs through SWIFT MT103/MT202 against conforming documents. For open-account disbursements, the LP should execute SWIFT MT103 wires with full beneficiary account details and invoice reference numbers. Canadian-dollar legs clear through Lynx, the high-value payment system, while U.S.-dollar legs may clear through the bank's New York correspondent. LC document packages must include commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, certificate of origin, fumigation certificate if required, insurance certificate, and third-party pre-shipment inspection report.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNH) with OSFI-regulated Schedule I banks under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to hedge long-term USD revenue streams and RMB procurement costs
Vanilla FX options, including zero-cost collars, used for committed trade flows
FX swaps for temporary liquidity conversion between CAD, USD, and offshore CNH

Offshore deliverable RMB (CNH) forwards where a Canadian bank is able to book and settle CNH exposures; non-deliverable RMB forwards are permissible only as embedded hedging for on-shore CNY settlement risk, must be approved by the LP's treasury committee, and cannot be used for speculative yield generation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 15 of each year for information current as at December 31 of the preceding year; if the Registrar assigns an anniversary-based filing date, within 60 days of that anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty assessed under the legal publicity regime; repeated non-compliance permits the Registrar to administratively radiate the registration, resulting in loss of legal publicity protection and inability to invoke rights in Quebec courts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) and related provincial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following a December 31 fiscal year end; for non-calendar fiscal periods, five months after the fiscal period end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 100 per month per T5013 form, capped at CAD 2,500; gross negligence penalties up to 5% of reported amounts plus interest and possible prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is compulsory for a limited partnership under Quebec law; audit or review engagements become mandatory only if imposed by the partnership agreement, a lender, a bulk purchaser, or a securities regulator.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook; IFRS is permitted if elected by the general partner.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual declaration confirms the general partners and persons with power to bind the limited partnership. Individual limited partners are not separately listed in the annual declaration; however, the partnership must maintain an internal UBO/contribution register, update it within 30 days of any transfer, and produce it upon the Registrar's audit request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners' Contributions and Withdrawals
Register of General Partners and Powers of Representation
Minute and Resolution Book for General Partner Decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 225–850 typical annual fee for a Quebec registered agent or domiciliary service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: For annual review engagement: USD 2,500–5,500; for full audit: USD 6,000–15,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Quebec general corporate reference rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); the Quebec LP is fiscally transparent and not charged to corporate income tax—partners are taxed on allocated income at their respective corporate or individual rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday in Canada or Quebec. Preferential deductions include the federal small business deduction for Canadian-controlled private corporations (9% federal / 4% Quebec) ineligible at LP level, zero-rated GST/HST on export sales of Baijiu liquor, accelerated capital cost allowances for qualifying manufacturing/processing assets, SR&ED tax credits where applicable, and the Canada-China DTA foreign tax credit for Chinese resident partners.
